info.title: MediSync Connect API
info.summary: One API for every practice and hospital system MediSync Connect reaches.
info.description:
Connect moves data between apps (MediSync Scribe, MediSync Dictate, partner apps) and practice or hospital systems (PVS, KIS).

Rules that do not change within v1:
- One operation per verb. Reads are `GET`. A write is a plan (`POST .../plans/{verb}`), then a transfer (`POST /transfers`) with the release of the person who reviewed the plan.
- Every write is a draft that a person released. Connect and the hub refuse a write without a release.
- Call `capabilities.get` to learn what a connection supports. A verb the connection cannot do fails with `verb_unsupported`; no verb answers an empty list for "not supported".
- Changes are additive only. Clients ignore unknown fields and accept unknown enum values and error codes.
- Every error has the same body: `{ "error": { "type", "code", "message", "request_id", ... } }`.
- A request body with a top-level field its schema does not have answers 400 `invalid_request` with `param` naming the field.

Test sites: a site made with a test key has a simulated hub inside Connect (`Site.simulated_hub`). It approves the app's grants at once, answers reads with invented patients, plans with the real planner and reports a released transfer as written. It never reaches a PVS or KIS. Every answer it gave carries `simulated: true` and the header `MediSync-Simulated: true`. A live site never has one.

Partners call `https://api.medisync.me/v1/connect/...` with their `msk_live_` or `msk_test_` key as a bearer token. The key needs the Connect scope of the operation, and MediSync Connect must be turned on for the key's project in the console. The system catalogue (`systems.list`, `systems.get`) needs neither: any valid key reads it.

A partner app with its own key pair calls the same operations with an access token of MediSync Connect's authorization server instead of a key (`private_key_jwt`, `https://connect.medisync.me/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`). An app token acts as the app's project; an installation token acts only at the site of its installation.

Errors come in two bodies with the same `error.type`, `error.code`, `error.message` and `error.request_id`: Connect's own (`ErrorEnvelope`), and the gateway's (`GatewayError`) for its checks (key, scope, switch, limits), for a timeout and for every 5xx.

post.summary: Request a grant: app × verbs × roles at a site
post.description: The grant stays `pending` until the practice admin approves it in the hub. At a live site only an app that MediSync verified asks, and only for verbs and roles within its verification: 403 `forbidden` with `reason: app_not_verified` or `not_verified_verb` else. A verified app holds its verified verbs already where it made the site or the practice linked it.

get.summary: List the organisation's apps
get.description: The console lists the apps of the organisation it names. An API key lists only the app of its own project.

get.summary: Get an app
get.description: The console reads any app of the organisation it names. An API key reads only the app of its own project; any other app answers 404.

patch.description: An API key of the app's own project changes the texts the practice admin reads, the links, the redirect URIs and the JWKS URL. At an app with a live project only a key of that live project does: a test key answers 403 `forbidden` with `reason: test_key`, a key of another project 404. The JWKS URL must be https on a host whose every address is public. The scopes, the verbs, the projects and the status change in the console only. An access token cannot call it.

post.summary: Add a public key for client authentication
post.description: A public key for `private_key_jwt` (RFC 7523): an EC P-256 key (ES256) or an Ed25519 key (EdDSA), as a JWK or as a PEM (SPKI). Never a private key: a key with a private part answers 400. Without `kid` the key id is the JWK thumbprint (RFC 7638). An app holds up to 5 keys. Add the new key, switch your signer, then delete the old key. Only a key of the app's own project adds or deletes keys, and at an app with a live project only a key of that live project (else 403 `test_key`, or 404 for another project), or the console.

delete.summary: Delete a key of an app
delete.description: Assertions signed with the key fail from now on. Access tokens already issued keep working until they expire (15 minutes).

get.summary: Get an installation with its authorization

delete.summary: Uninstall the app at a site
delete.description: Ends the installation and every grant of it. The app's calls at the site stop at once, and the hub drops the grants. A new install needs a new link on the practice's hub PC, or a new site.

post.summary: Ask the site admin for more verbs
post.description: A pending grant at the installation's site. The site admin decides on the hub; the simulated hub of a test site approves at once. Approved verbs add up: the installation keeps what it had. One request waits at a time; a second answers 409 `conflict`. At a live site only within the app's verification: 403 `forbidden` with `reason: app_not_verified` or `not_verified_verb` else.

post.summary: Revoke an app at the site, for the practice
post.description: The site owner ends any app's installation at the site, MediSync's own included: the app that set the site up, or MediSync. `revoked_by` is an active admin of the site; a partner sends that admin's member assertion (`admin_assertion`), as for a role change. The app's calls and tokens at the site stop at once, the hub drops its grants, and a new verification of the app does not bring it back. Only a new link on the practice's hub PC does. The practice admin does the same in the MediSync Connect window (Apps). An app ends its own installation with `installations.delete`. Addition of 05.11.2026.

post.summary: Start adding the app to a practice's hub
post.description: A practice that runs a hub adds the app to its site on the hub PC: the app's backend makes a link here and hands the code to the app on that PC, which gives it to the hub (`host.link` of the Connect Runtime). The hub claims the code with its own token, which names the site. The code lives 10 minutes and is shown once. A partner app must be verified by MediSync for a live link. A MediSync service token links MediSync's own app for the organisation it acts for. Use an app token or a key, not an installation token. Addition of 05.11.2026.

get.summary: Read an app link
get.description: After the hub claimed the code: the site, the hub PC's device name and the check number of its device key. The app on the hub PC shows the number the hub gave it; the practice admin compares the two before the backend approves. Addition of 05.11.2026.

post.summary: Approve an app link with the hub's device proof
post.description: The hub's own proof that the practice linked the app on its PC (`host.device_proof` with the `lnk_` id, valid 60 seconds). The answer carries the installation: active, with the verbs MediSync verified (MediSync's app: its feature rights). This is the practice's authorization of the app as data controller. It needs no other consent. `conflict` with `reason` when no hub claimed the link, it expired, or the claiming hub is no longer the site's hub; `forbidden` with `reason: other_device` for a proof of another device. Addition of 05.11.2026.

200.description: The link, approved, with the installation.

get.description: Runs the mapping rules of `mappings.propose` for every template the caller may use with this connection (MediSync's library, the system templates of its system and the tenant's own) and ranks them. `clean` means every section has a slot of its own. `unused_slots` names slots of the system that no section of the template fills.

post.summary: Create a mapping or its next version
post.description: A mapping belongs to the caller that made it. Only that caller makes its next version (`mapping_id`); another app's mapping answers 404, also at a shared site. A mapping from before 06.11.2026 belongs to the app that set the site up.

get.description: The caller's own mapping only; another app's mapping answers 404. A write without `mapping_id` uses the caller's own newest mapping of the connection.

post.summary: Propose a mapping from section titles
post.description: Deterministic rules per system first, against the slots of the connection's snapshot: the slot's own name, its label, a synonym group (Anamnese, Vorgeschichte, Subjektiv), the kind (the diagnosis list), the single slot of a system that takes one document. A slot outside the snapshot is never named. A section no rule places goes to `fallback_slot` and is listed in `sections` with the reason `fallback`. Every rule has a `confidence` and a `reason`. The answer is a draft; a person confirms it with `mappings.create`, which pins the template version and `snapshot_hash`.

example.note: A proposal is a draft. A person confirms it with mappings.create.

post.summary: Upload a PDF for `document.attach`
post.description: Multipart, up to 25 MB, a PDF. Sealed to the hub of `site_id` at once (HPKE, like a delivery); the cloud keeps no file name. Deleted when the transfer that carries it reaches a final state, or after 24 h. Once a plan with the upload is released, it stays at least until the transfer's `expires_at`, so the hub can retry and a person can resend; a transfer that failed on the hub keeps it until then too. After that a retry or resend answers `uploads_gone`.

site_id.description: The site whose hub gets the file. The cloud seals the file to that hub at once and cannot read it back. Required: an upload without it answers 400.

post.summary: Release a plan and send it
post.description: Takes a plan and the release of the person who reviewed it. Answers 202 at once; the hub delivers when online. Poll `transfers.get` or read events. Checks: licence, grant, role, practitioner link, plan age and adapter version, dedupe.

Location.description: URL of the transfer status resource.

post.summary: Settle an `in_doubt` or `failed` transfer
post.description: A person checked the target system: `mark_done` if the entry is there, `resend` to send it again, `mark_failed` to give it up. The answer is the settled transfer, or for `resend` the new one. A `failed` transfer is parked on the hub too: `mark_done` and `mark_failed` unpark it there; it has no release any more, so `resend` answers 409 and the note is released again. The PDFs of the plan (`uploads.create`) stay until the transfer's `expires_at`; a `resend` after they are gone answers 409 `uploads_gone`, and the transfer stays as it was. `resolved_by` is an active doctor or site admin; another role gets 403 `forbidden` with `reason` `role`.

get.summary: Get a setup session and the pairing its link made
get.description: The page that made the link polls this while the person sets up. Once the desk traded the link (`status: redeemed`), `pairing` is the hub pairing it made, with the device that claimed it. A site admin approves that pairing by name with `pairings.approve` (control 2): the link alone approves nothing. The link's token is never returned.

get.summary: Get the signed runtime and links to download it
get.description:
The Connect Runtime is the MediSync Connect hub without the desk, which a partner installs with its own product (MediSync Connect docs, Runtime). The runtime files are not public: this operation answers the signed manifest of the channel and download links for the runtime files of one platform, valid for 5 minutes. Only the hub and the HL7 listener of that platform, and on Linux the systemd units. Never a desk, the planner or an invitation setup.

Check `manifest_signature` over `manifest` with the MediSync update key before you use a file, and each file's SHA-256 and size against the manifest. The package `@medisyncai/connect-runtime` does both. A live key needs a usable Connect licence of the organisation; a test key does not.

get.summary: Context changes for a member
get.description: Without `connection_id` the cloud asks every connection of the site that can run `context.events` at once and merges the answers, oldest first. Events with the same time keep the order of the connections (oldest connection first) and the order each system gave. Every event names the connection it came from. A connection that fails does not fail the call while another one answers.

get.summary: Appointments of a site in a date range
get.description: Every connection of the site that can run `appointment.list` is asked at once (or only `connection_id`), and the answers are merged by start time. Each item names its connection and system. `sources` says per connection whether it answered: the caller keeps its own copy of a connection's appointments when that connection's source is not `ok`. DURIA lists booked appointments per patient only, so it answers for the given `patient_ids` and says `needs_patient_ids` without them. A connection that fails does not fail the call while another one answers.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD, German time). At most 31 days after `from`.

get.summary: Search patients in the target system
Read one patient
get.description: The patient as the system holds it. Answered by the system through the site's hub; nothing is stored. Check `capabilities.get` first: `partial` names its `limits`. 403 `forbidden` with `reason: needs_kontext`: the system answers only for the patient open in it (MEDICAL OFFICE, QUINCY, T2med); the message names the person's step, and the same call works after it. The same answer comes for another patient than the open one and for an export file older than the connection allows. 404 `not_found`: the system has no such record. 422 `verb_unsupported` or `verb_unverified`: the connection cannot run the verb. 503 `agent_offline`: the hub is offline.

MemberQuery.description: The member the request runs for. Context and reads go only to this member.

PatientIds.name: patient_ids
PatientIds.description: Comma-separated patient ids of the system, at most 50. DURIA lists booked appointments per patient only; the other systems filter by them.

SlotIdsQuery.name: slot_ids
SlotIdsQuery.description: Only entries of these slots of `record.slots`, comma-separated. DURIA asks only these text groups. Every system gets the same filter on `slot_id` in the hub. Addition of 11.11.2026.

KennzeichenQuery.name: kennzeichen
KennzeichenQuery.description: Only entries with one of these Textkennzeichen or meanings, comma-separated: `A,B`, `finding` or `DD,diagnosis_acute`. A value matches an entry's `kennzeichen` or its `meaning`, so meanings work on every system that fills `meaning`. The hub applies the filter the same way for every system. Addition of 11.11.2026.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Unique key per logical request, for example a UUID. A repeat with the same key and body returns the first answer; with another body it returns `idempotency_conflict`. Kept 24 h.

IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: Unique key per logical request, for example a UUID. A repeat with the same key and body returns the first answer; with another body it returns `idempotency_conflict`. Kept 24 h. Required here: it protects a practice record from a double write.

error.message: name is required
No valid credential.

Forbidden.description: Missing scope, verb not granted, or no licence.

error.message: The key lacks the scope connect.transfer.
The practice admin has not granted record.write to this app.
All 25 seats of the DURIA licence are used this month.
The resource does not exist or belongs to another tenant.
The adapter changed from duria@1.2.0 to duria@1.3.0. Plan again.
This document was transferred to this patient before.
The Idempotency-Key was used before with a different request body.

Unprocessable.description: The connection cannot do this verb, or the release does not match.

error.message: MEDICAL OFFICE cannot receive coded diagnoses over GDT.
record.write is not proven on QUINCY WIN. Use a test key or ask for the pilot flag.
The patient in the release differs from the patient in the plan.
The body is over the limit: 5 MB for JSON, 25 MB for uploads.
Too many requests. Wait `retry_after` seconds.
An error on our side. Retrying with the same Idempotency-Key is safe.
transfers.create is not implemented yet.
The practice or hospital system answered with an error. `target_error` carries the vendor code.
The hub could not reach the system.
The hub for this site is offline. Reads cannot run. Writes queue instead (202).
The service is starting, overloaded or in maintenance.

GatewayTimeout.description: Connect did not answer within 60 seconds. A repeat with the same Idempotency-Key is safe.

ErrorCode.description: Stable error code. Codes are only added, never renamed or removed. Treat an unknown code like its HTTP status.

message.description: English text for developers. Not for end users, may change.

param.description: The parameter or body field that failed validation, as a JSON pointer or name.

reason.description: Capability reason, for example `system_cannot`, `protocol_cannot`, `not_tested`. With `forbidden`, `member_secret` means the member has not linked their own account of the system in MediSync Connect (DURIA); `admin_assertion_required` means a partner key sent no valid `admin_assertion`; `other_device` means no valid `device_proof`; `not_site_setup` means only the app that set up the site (or MediSync) may change this, and an installed app changes only the members it added; `test_key` means a test key may not change an app that has a live project; `app_not_verified` means MediSync has not verified the app for live sites, `no_app` that the project has no app; `role` means the member's role may not do this; `needs_kontext` means the system answers only for the patient open in it, and the message names the step for that system (T2med needs the patient opened in T2med and MediSync started there, MEDICAL OFFICE needs the patient open in MEDICAL OFFICE or MediSync started from its Krankenblatt, QUINCY needs the MediSync button of the BDT-Anschluss pressed in the patient's Karteikarte); a read for another patient than the open one, or after the export file is older than the connection allows, gets the same reason; the call may succeed later. `no_desk_session` means the system reads for the member only through their MediSync Connect desk (T2med) and the member has no desk session at the site; the call may succeed after the member signs in to the desk.

retryable.description: True when the same request may succeed later.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before a retry.

message.description: Vendor message, scrubbed of patient data.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The one error body of the API. The gateway passes it through unchanged.

Verb.description: A Connect verb. New verbs are added over time; clients must accept unknown values.

WriteVerb.description: A verb that writes into the target system. It always goes plan, release, transfer.

EventType.description: Event type. New types are added over time.

Role.description: Role of a member at a site.

VerbStatus.description: `proven`: ran against the real system. `built`: code exists, tested on the simulator or not at all. `planned`: spec only. `not_possible`: the system or protocol cannot do it. `unknown`: not known yet.

LicenceType.description: `included`: no partner charge. `per_user`: per active user per month. `per_site`: per site per month.

oneOf.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. `null` on the last page.

placement.description: `hub`: the adapter runs in the hub inside the practice or hospital network. `cloud`: it runs in Connect.

proof.description: Strongest proof that we can talk to the system.

licence_type.description: Licence type of the connector. `tbd` until decided.

verbs.description: Status per verb. Verbs not listed are `unknown`.

note.description: Short public remark on the system, for example a limit of the vendor interface.

practice_id.description: The practice that owns the site (`prc_`). One hub per site serves every app installed there.

access.description: `setup`: the caller made the site (or is MediSync) and sets it up: members, pairing, connections, setup links. `installation`: the caller reaches it through its app's installation: reads, its own members (never an admin), plans and transfers with its verbs.

pilot.description: Set by MediSync staff. On a pilot site a live key may call a verb whose status is `unverified`; elsewhere only a test key may.

beta_invited.description: Set by MediSync staff. The setup link of an invited site offers the download of the Connect beta.

simulated_hub.description: The site's hub is the simulated hub of a test site: it approves the app's grants at once, answers reads with invented data, and reports every released transfer as written. It never reaches a PVS or KIS. Every test site gets one until a real hub pairs there. Always false on a live site.

delivery_ttl_hours.description: Set by MediSync staff. Hours a queued transfer waits for the hub of this site before it expires. Null means the default of 24 hours.

metadata.description: Up to 20 keys for the caller. No patient data.

practice_id.description: Another location of a practice whose site the caller set up. Left out: a new practice that owns the site.

simulated.description: Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.

oneOf.description: Practitioner id in the target system. Only a site admin sets it.

agent_id.description: The approved hub of the site (`agt_`). Only it redeems the ticket.

ticket.description: The one-time ticket. Shown once; Connect keeps only its hash. Hand it to the desk of the member on the hub's PC, never to a log.

role.description: A new role drops the practitioner link. A partner key sends `admin_assertion` with it.

set_by.description: Member id of the site admin. With `admin_assertion` it must be the admin of the assertion.

AdminAssertion.description: The member assertion of an active admin of the site, as MediSync Connect on the PC holds it after the admin signed in. A partner key sends it for a change the hub enforces (a practitioner link, a new role); without it the call answers 403 `forbidden` with `reason` `admin_assertion_required`. MediSync's own servers do not send it. An admin without an assertion makes the change in MediSync Connect on the PC.

DeviceProof.description: The hub's proof that it approves its own pairing. MediSync Connect on the PC makes it. The cloud checks the signature with the device key of the pairing, `ts` within 60 seconds and a new nonce.

sig.description:
Ed25519 with the device key over `connect-hub-approve
` + agent_id + `
` + pairing id + `
` + ts + `
` + nonce, standard base64.

RuntimeRelease.description: The signed manifest of a channel and the runtime files of one platform (MediSync Connect docs, Runtime).

manifest.description: The bytes of `manifest.json`, standard base64. Verify them unchanged: the signature covers `medisync-connect-manifest v1\n` followed by these bytes.

manifest_signature.description: The bytes of `manifest.json.sig`, standard base64: `{key_id, sig}`, an Ed25519 signature with a MediSync update key.

sha256.description: From the manifest. Check the download against it.

url.description: A download link valid for 5 minutes. Send no credential with it.

last_seen_at.description: The last time the agent showed it is there: its hello, a pong or a frame while online (at most about a minute old then), its goodbye or the lost socket when offline. Null: never connected.

oneOf.description: Shown once at creation, then `null`. 8 characters, 10 minutes. The cloud takes 10 pairing attempts per client address and minute, and refuses a code for 10 minutes after 5 failed attempts with it.
The device that claimed the code. The admin checks it before approving.

check_number.description: Once a device claimed the pairing. 16 hex digits in four groups, from the device key. MediSync Connect shows the same number on the PC; the admin compares the two before approving.

requested_by.description: Member id of the site admin.

approved_by.description: Member id of the site admin.

simulated.description: Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.

status.description: `offline`: the site's hub is offline (socket closed, two missed pings, or `hub.goodbye`). Active again after the next `hub.hello`.

oneOf.description: Version the hub read from the system.

settings.description: Non-secret settings. Credentials stay in the hub and never pass this API.

system_id.description: The catalogue's system id, which is the hub adapter id (`medical-office`, `quincy`, `medisoftware`, `t2med`, `duria`).

settings.description: The keys of the adapter's settings form that are not secret, in the form's names. At most 16 KB. T2med: `aps_origin` only, never `aps_cert_sha256`. Keys the form does not know are ignored and named in `ignored`.

source.description: Where the settings come from, for the audit log.

simulated.description: Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.

agent_id.description: The hub that took the settings.

status.description: `created`: the hub probed and keeps the connection. `exists`: the site or the hub has a connection of this system; nothing changed. `refused`: see `reason`; nothing changed.

reason.description: For `refused`. From the cloud: `duplicate`, `unknown_system`, `not_a_hub_system`, `agent_offline`. From the hub: `carry_over_closed` (no local admin allowed it), `adapter_unknown`, `secret_refused`, `pin_refused`, `invalid_settings` (see `param`), `credential_needed` (the system needs a connection password), `probe_failed` (see `error_code`), `credential_missing` (MediSync's vendor key has not reached the hub).

error_code.description: The error code of the failed probe.

certificate.description: T2med: the certificate the hub pinned at this first contact.

needs.description: What a person still adds: `member_accounts` (DURIA: every person links their own account in the desk).

ignored.description: Settings keys the adapter's form does not know.

approved_by.description: The member id of the site admin who approves.

simulated.description: Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.
Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.

agent_offline_reason.description: Only while the hub is offline. `update` means it comes back within minutes.

roles.description: Roles that may release this verb. Empty for reads.

simulated.description: Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.

id.description: The project of a partner key, as before apps, or the name of a MediSync app.

app_id.description: The registered app (`app_…`) of a partner grant.

vendor_name.description: The company behind the app, as the practice admin sees it in the hub.

installation_id.description: The installation this grant belongs to. Null for a MediSync app.

status.description: A grant is `pending` until the practice admin approves or denies it in the hub. A `denied` grant lets the app ask again. The practice admin can also revoke an approved grant in the hub.

app_id.description: The app that asks. A partner key leaves it out: Connect sets the key's project. A partner key that names another app gets 403 `forbidden`. A MediSync app names itself.

vendor_name.description: The company behind the app. The practice admin sees it when deciding. MediSync apps default to MediSync GmbH.

name.description: The name the practice admin sees when deciding.

avv_url.description: The data processing agreement (AVV) the practice signs with the vendor.

redirect_uris.description: Kept for a later browser flow; Connect uses none today (no consent page since 05.11.2026). https, a loopback `http://127.0.0.1/...` or `http://[::1]/...` (any port matches, RFC 8252), or a private-use scheme such as `com.example.app:/callback`.

jwks_uri.description: The app's JWKS URL (https) for `private_key_jwt`, next to or instead of uploaded keys.

keys.description: Uploaded public keys, without the key material.

scopes.description: The most a token of the app can hold.

verbs.description: The verbs the app may ask a site for.

projects.description: The console project the app acts as, per environment. Its sites are the sites of these projects.

created_via.description: `console`, or `grant`: made for a project that asked for a grant with its key before it had an app.

verification.description: MediSync's verification of the app: the verbs and roles it gets where it is installed. Null: not verified. An unverified app gets no installation at a live site.

jwk.description: A public JWK, `kty` `EC` with `crv` `P-256`, or `kty` `OKP` with `crv` `Ed25519`.

pem.description: A public key in SPKI PEM form (`-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----`).

AuthorizationDetail.description: RFC 9396 authorization details of the type `medisync_connect`: verbs and the roles that may release them, at one site.

status.description: `pending` at a test site until the first request is approved, `active` while a grant is approved (a verified app: from the start), `revoked` after an uninstall, a revocation by the practice, or when the last approved grant was revoked.

authorization_details.description: What the app may do at the site now. The union of its approved grants.

pending_requests.description: Requests that wait for the site admin.

consented_via.description: How the installation came about: `creator` (the app made the site), `link` (the practice linked it on its hub PC), `hub` (the site admin approved a request on the hub), `simulated` (a test site), `migrated` (older data). `hosted` is no longer made.

revoked_by_practice.description: The practice ended it (desk, hub or the site owner). A new verification does not bring it back.

app.description: The app, as the practice sees it.

revoked_by.description: The active admin of the site who revokes the app.

admin_assertion.description: A partner sends the member assertion of `revoked_by`; MediSync's servers signed the person in themselves.

verbs.description: The verbs and the roles that may release them, a subset of the app's `verbs`.

code.description: Shown once, in the answer of `appLinks.create`.

site.description: The site of the hub that claimed the code.

device.description: The hub PC that claimed the code.

check_number.description: The check number of the claiming hub's device key, 16 hex digits in four groups. The hub shows the same number to the app.

owner.description: `medisync`: MediSync's library or a system template, read only. `tenant`: the caller's own.

section_id.description: Section of the document or template.

oneOf.description: The template version the mapping was made for.
SHA-256 of the slots the mapping was made against (`mappings.propose`). Another hash today means the system's slots changed.

fallback_slot.description: Slot for sections without a rule.

mapping_id.description: Set to create the next version of an existing mapping.

template_version.description: Pins this version of the template. Default the latest.

snapshot_hash.description: The `snapshot_hash` of the proposal the person confirmed. Default the hash of the connection's stored slots.

MappingProposalRequest.description: Send `template_id` or `sections`, one of the two.

sections.description: Section titles only. Send no clinical text.

note.description: A proposal is a draft. A person confirms it with `mappings.create`.

snapshot_hash.description: SHA-256 of the slots the proposal used. Pass it to `mappings.create`.

fallback_reason.description: Why this slot is the fallback. Clients treat an unknown value as `first_text_slot`.

sections.description: Every section, with its slot, including those that go to the fallback.

unused_slots.description: Writable slots no section fills, for a section the template could add.

clean.description: Every section has a slot of its own; nothing lands in the fallback.

PlacementReason.description: Why a section got its slot. `slot_id` the slot's own name, `label` its label, `synonym` a synonym group, `kind` the only slot of its kind (the diagnosis list), `single_slot` the system takes the whole document in one slot, `fallback` no slot fits, `no_slot` the system has no writable text slot. Clients treat an unknown value like `fallback`.

score.description: 0 to 1. Mean section confidence (three quarters) and the share of the system's slots the template fills (one quarter).

simulated.description: Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.
Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.

status.description: `supported`: may be called. `partial`: may be called, but only part of the verb works on this connection; `limits` says which part. `unverified`: built or planned, not proven here; refused with `verb_unverified` except on test keys and pilot sites. `unsupported`: refused with `verb_unsupported`.

limits.description: Only with `partial`. Short codes for the parts that do not work here, for example `no_diagnoses` or `text_categories_only`. New codes may appear; clients show unknown codes as text.

result.description: What a successful write proves: `confirmed` (the system acknowledged the entry) or `written` (file written, no acknowledgement).

idempotent.description: False: a timeout after send ends `in_doubt` and is not retried.

granted.description: The site admin granted this verb to the calling app.

licensed.description: The calling organisation holds an active licence for this connector.

pilot.description: Only with `unverified`: true when the site has the pilot flag, so a live key may call the verb there.

simulated.description: Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.

verbs.description: Every verb, including unsupported ones. A verb missing here is unsupported.

id.description: Patient id in the target system.

PatientRef.description: Patient reference. Name and birth date let the hub check the patient (control 9).

reviewed.description: Must be `true`: a clinician reviewed the code. Model suggestions are never sent.

ExportRange.description: The days the system's export file holds. MEDICAL OFFICE writes the Krankenblatt from the date the person chose in "Datenexport ab": entries before `from` are not in the answer because the file does not have them, not because the patient has none. Left out by systems that answer from their whole record. Addition of 11.11.2026.

system.description: `fallnummer`: the case number of the KIS (SAP IS-H `FALNR`, HL7 `PV1-19`). `encounter`: the id of a FHIR `Encounter`. Which one a connection looks up is a setting of the connection.

CaseRef.description: The hospital case or encounter a document or a billing proposal belongs to.

sections.description: Draft text. A person releases it before anything is written. A section with the id `connect:case` was the case number before `case_ref` existed; the hospital adapters still read it when `case_ref` is missing.

action.description: What the hub will do, for example `write_entry`, `write_file`, `book`.

simulated.description: Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.

adapter.description: Adapter pinned by the plan, `duria@1.2.0`. The hub refuses a different version with `plan_stale`.

mapping_id.description: The mapping the plan used. `null` for a verb that places no sections and planned without a mapping (diagnoses, documents, orders, appointments, referrals, billing).

plan_hash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the plan, 64 lower case hex digits. The release names it.

document_hash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the document, 64 lower case hex digits.

expires_at.description: 30 minutes after creation. Release before then.

case_ref.description: The hospital case the diagnoses belong to. A KIS over HL7 books diagnoses to a case (BAR^P12, PV1-19); without one the plan warns `case_missing` and writes nothing. Pass on the `case_ref` of `patient.context`. A practice system ignores it.

The hospital case the diagnosis lines belong to. A KIS that files documents into a case (PV1-19) needs it; without one the plan warns `case_missing` and writes nothing. Pass on the `case_ref` of `patient.context`. A practice system ignores it.

The hospital case the order belongs to. A KIS that books orders to a case needs it; without one the plan warns `case_missing` and writes nothing. Pass on the `case_ref` of `patient.context`. A practice system ignores it.

The hospital case the document belongs to. A KIS that files documents into a case (PV1-19) needs it; without one the plan warns `case_missing` and writes nothing. Pass on the `case_ref` of `patient.context`. With `render`, it fills `render.document.case_ref`; when both are sent they must be equal. A practice system ignores it.

render.description: The document as text for the target system, without a PDF. No hub renders a PDF yet, so `template` is not used yet, and the document carries no `attachments` (400 with `param` `render.document.attachments`); send a PDF as `upload_id` in its own plan.

case_ref.description: Names the kind of `case_id`. When both are sent, `case_ref.value` must equal `case_id`. Without it, `case_id` is a `fallnummer`.

date.description: The day the service was performed. Required by SAP IS-H.

factor.description: GOÄ multiplier (Steigerungsfaktor), for example 2.3. Above the site's threshold it needs a `justification` (GOÄ § 5 (2), § 12 (3)).

tariff.description: The service catalogue of the code in the target system (SAP IS-H `INHS_SRVCAT`, `TARID`). Default: the catalogue of the connection's settings.

practitioner_link.description: The member's practitioner link. Empty or absent when the member has none. That passes where the system lists no practitioners (GDT), and at a site that moved from the 0.7.x agent, where Connect uses the hub's proposal or the practice default doctor, else signs `write_as: connection`.

transfer_id.description: Set when a desk signed the release; the desk chose the id.

ReleaseInput.description: Who released what. Without `sig`, Connect signs the release and the hub still checks the member against its roster.

write_as.description: Set by Connect instead of a practitioner link, only at a site that moved from the 0.7.x agent, for a member without a link: the entry is written with the connection's own account, as the old agent wrote it (DURIA practice account, T2med kontext user). Absent on every other release.

TransferStatus.description: `queued` → `delivered` → `completed`, `partially_completed`, `in_doubt` or `failed`. A queued transfer that is not delivered within 24 h ends `expired` and is free. Since 09.11.2026 a transfer that reached the hub but waits there for a step of a person shows `queued` again, with `status_reason` (for example `needs_kontext`) and `waiting_for`; it is not on its way to the system until that step is done.

simulated.description: Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.

waiting_for.description: Present only while the transfer waits at the hub for a step of a person; `status` is then `queued`. `patient_context`, with `status_reason: needs_kontext`: T2med writes only for the patient opened from T2med, so a member opens the patient in T2med and the hub writes then. Values may be added. Addition of 09.11.2026.

release.description: The signed release. In every transfer answer `patient_confirmed` names the patient by `id` only; names and birth date go only to the hub. The cloud deletes the plan content and the full release when the transfer reaches a final state (`completed`, `partially_completed`, `failed`, `expired`, or settled with `transfers.resolve`).

desk_id.description: The id the desk app made for itself at install, `dsk_` prefix.

assertion.description: Compact JWT, `alg: EdDSA`, `typ: connect-desk+jwt`. Claims: `iss` connect, `aud` connect-desk, `sub` member id, `site`, `role`, `desk`, `name`, `site_name`, `site_kind`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti`.

key_id.description: The Connect key that signed it, as the hub pins it.

started_by.description: `setup_link`: the desk started it for a setup link after the person pressed "Mit MediSync anmelden" on the link page (`/s/<token>`). The page asks whether to connect this PC (`desk_name`) as the Connect server of `site_name`, and offers no other practice. Absent for a desk's own sign-in. Addition of 11.11.2026.

site_name.description: The practice of the setup link, with `started_by` only. Addition of 11.11.2026 (security review F4).

oneOf.description: The PC's name as the desk sent it. Show it to the person; do not trust it as proof.

The site of the member who approved the sign-in. While the sign-in is pending: the site the desk last worked for (its session, migration ticket, join or first traded setup link), so the page can preselect that practice. Either only to a token of the dashboard the site belongs to; any other caller gets null for a pending sign-in and 404 for an approved one. Pending value: addition of 11.11.2026.

expires_at.description: The end of the 10 minutes in which the person may finish the sign-in.

external_ref.description: The person's MediSync user id. Unique per site.

desk_id.description: `null` for a sign-in of a setup link page.

redirect_to.description: Where to send the browser. It carries the one-time code; never log it.

action.description: `mark_done`: the person checked the target system and the entry is there. `resend`: send again, under a new transfer id with a release Connect signs again; a desk-signed release cannot be signed again and the transfer ends `failed` with `desk_release_needed`. `mark_failed`: the entry is not there and is not sent again. In every case the hub hears of it and the queue of the patient goes on.

site_id.description: The site whose hub the file is sealed to.

expires_at.description: Deleted on delivery or after 24 h.

case_ref.description: The hospital case the patient is in, when the system names one (HL7 ADT: PV1-19). A KIS files a document into a case: pass it on as `case_ref` of the document, or of the request of `diagnosis.write`, `diagnosis.write.text`, `document.attach` and `medication.order`.

simulated.description: Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.

connection_id.description: The connection the context came from. `null` when `context` is `null`.

system_id.description: The system of that connection. `null` when `context` is `null`.

PatientContextResponse.description: `context` is `null` when no patient is open for the member.

case_ref.description: The hospital case of the event, when the system names one (HL7 ADT: PV1-19).

connection_id.description: The connection the event came from. The event `id` is unique only together with it.

simulated.description: Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.
Present and true when the simulated hub of a test site gave this answer. No real system was reached.

insured_kind.description: BDT systems: field 3108 as written, `M` member, `F` family member, `R` pensioner. Other systems leave it out.

status.description: BDT systems: the Versichertenstatus (field 4112) as written, for example `1000` or `5000`. Other systems leave it out.

vknr.description: BDT systems: the VKNR of the statutory insurer (field 4104). Other systems leave it out.

RecordEntry.description: One entry of the patient's record as the system holds it. Every system fills the required fields. `kennzeichen`, `meaning`, `source` and `field` are filled where the system has them (the BDT systems MEDICAL OFFICE and QUINCY) and left out elsewhere. Clients must accept entries without them. Addition of 11.11.2026.

id.description: Stable for the same entry of the same file or system answer. Holds no patient data.

slot_id.description: The slot of `record.slots` the entry belongs to, when it belongs to one a write can target. Filter with `slot_ids`.

slot_label.description: The name the system shows for the entry's kind, for example `Anamnese (A)` or `Freitext`.

kennzeichen.description: The system's Textkennzeichen of the entry (QUINCY: `A`, `B`, `DD`, ...), null when the entry has none. Systems without Kennzeichen leave it out. Filter with `kennzeichen`.

meaning.description: What the entry is, the same words for every system: `anamnesis`, `finding`, `therapy`, `diagnosis_acute`, `diagnosis_permanent`, `medication`, `other`. Taken from the Kennzeichen (QUINCY) or from the field or category name (MEDICAL OFFICE). New values may appear; treat an unknown value as `other`. Filter with `kennzeichen`.

source.description: Where in the system's data the text stood. BDT systems: `field` (a standard text field, see `field`), `result` (the text of a GDT result), `category` (a free category), and for QUINCY how the category named its Kennzeichen: `category_code` (`A`), `category_code_name` (`A#Anamnese`) or `category_name` (`Anamnese`). New values may appear.

field.description: BDT systems only. The BDT field that opened the text, for example 6220 (Befund) or 6330 (the first free category).

prescription.description: MEDICAL OFFICE: the kind of the prescription as written, `K` Kassenrezept, `G` grünes Rezept, `P` Privatrezept. Other systems leave it out.

kennzeichen.description: QUINCY only. The Textkennzeichen of the line, null for a 6210 or 6211 line.

source.description: BDT systems only. Where the line stood: `6210` (Verordnung), `6211` (other medication) or the `source` of a record entry (a Kennzeichen of meaning `medication`).

reference_range.description: The normal range as the system wrote it (BDT field 8460), for example `3.5 - 5.1`.

interpretation.description: The flag the system set on the value, null when it set none.

patient_name.description: The patient's name as the system has it ("Nachname, Vorname"), when it gives one. Hub 0.1.4-beta.30 and later.

patient_birth_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, when the system gives it. Hub 0.1.4-beta.30 and later.

title.description: The appointment's own text in the system (MEDICAL OFFICE the SUMMARY of the Terminzone entry).

practitioner.description: The calendar or column the appointment is in (DURIA), when the system names one.

connection_id.description: The connection the appointment came from. Set in `appointments.listSite`.

system_id.description: The system of that connection. Set in `appointments.listSite`.

kind.description: Who pays, for a practice case. `pkv`: private billing (GOÄ). A PVS that does not show the payer of a private case, such as T2med, reports a self-payer as `pkv` too; `self` only when the PVS names the patient as payer. `hospital`: a case of a hospital information system (SAP IS-H Fall) that the hospital bills itself; the payer is not part of it.

case_ref.description: The case as `billing.propose` takes it (`fallnummer` for SAP IS-H).

factor.description: GOÄ multiplier, where the system keeps one.

tariff.description: Service catalogue of the code in the system (SAP IS-H `TARID`).

case_pseudonym.description: HMAC(BSNR, case number, quarter) with a hub-only key.

BillingExport.description: Aggregates and pseudonymous findings only. No patient leaves the practice.

oneOf.description: Per user: active users per month. Per site: sites. `null`: no cap.

site_ids.description: Sites the licence is activated for. Empty means every site of the organisation.

LicenceCreate.description: `included` is for MediSync's own organisation only; any other organisation answers 400.

active_users.description: Members who released at least one transfer or ran one read through this connector in the month (Europe/Berlin).

sites.description: Sites with at least one active user.

reads.description: Reads through this connector in the month.

transfers.description: Transfers released through this connector in the month.

billable_units.description: The invoice unit of the month. `per_user`, active users; `per_site`, sites; `included`, 0.

url.description: Works once, for one hour. It opens a short page whose button starts the desk at `medisync-connect://setup`, which trades it for a hub pairing code of the site.

status.description: `open` until the desk trades the link, then `redeemed`. `expired` after one hour without a trade.

requested_by.description: The site admin who made the session. The pairing is requested in this admin's name.

pairing.description: The hub pairing the link made, `null` before the trade. Approve it with `pairings.approve`, unless `approval` is `auto`.

approval.description: How the pairing gets approved (addition of 11.11.2026). `null` before the trade. `pending`: a site admin signed in on the link page and the desk on that PC traded it; the hub's claim is approved at once if it comes with the device key that desk named, within 10 minutes. `auto`: the link approved it, the pairing is `approved`, the PC is connected. `manual`: a site admin approves on the PC after comparing the check number, as before; `approval_reason` says why.

approval_reason.description: Why a person approves. `not_signed_in`: the link was opened without a sign-in. `not_admin`: the person who signed in is no active admin of this site. `no_device_key`: an older desk traded it. `other_device`: another device than the one that opened the link claimed the pairing. `link_old`: the link was older than 30 minutes, or the hub claimed more than 10 minutes after the trade. `second_claim`: someone used the link again after the trade. `hub_replaced`: an approved hub of the site was revoked within 24 hours.

signed_in_by.description: The member who signed in on the link page, `null` without a sign-in. With `auto` this member approved the hub.

contested.description: Someone used the link again after it was traded. Show it to the admin; the pairing waits for a person.

requested_by.description: An active admin of the site. The hub pairing the link makes is requested by this admin, as with `pairings.create`. Required: a request without it answers 400.

type.description: The class of error. Switch on this in code.

code.description: The exact reason. Stable; listed on the errors page.

message.description: A sentence for a person. It can change; do not parse it.

param.description: The parameter or header the error is about, if any.

request_id.description: The same as the outer `request_id`. MediSync Connect errors carry it only here, so read `error.request_id` to handle both.

retryable.description: True when the same request may succeed later.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before a retry.

message.description: Vendor message, scrubbed of patient data.

GatewayError.description: The gateway's error body: its own checks before Connect (401, 403 `missing_scope` and `product_not_enabled`, 404 `unknown_route`, 413, 429), a timeout (504), and every 5xx of Connect, which keeps Connect's `code` where the contract lists it.
